On the 20$\times$20 board the only material is in the right hand corner.
In the usual letter/number notation put

* $I16=B,\;I17=W,\;I18=W,\;I19=W,\;I20=B$,
* $J13=B,\;J14=B,\;J15=W,\;J16=W,\;J17=W,\;J18=W,\;J19=W,\;J20=B$,
* $K15\!-\!K19=W$, $L15\!-\!L19=W$,
* $M16=B,\;M17=W,\;M18=W,\;M19=W$, $N16=B,\;N17=W,\;N18=W,\;N19=W$,
* $O18=B,\;O19=B,\;O20=W$,

and the three isolated $F16,G16,H16=B$.  Up to symmetry this is the
whole of the position.

Put a black disc on the empty square $H18$, i.e. row $H$ column $18$.
In the $W$ direction

* $S$ : $I18,W$ $J18,W$ $K18,W$ $L18,W$ $M18,W$ $N18,W$ $O18,B$
  the six white discs $I18\!-\!N18$ are bounded below by the black
  disc $O18$;
* $SE$ : $I19,W$ $J20,B$
  the white disc $I19$ is bounded on the $SE$ diagonal by the black
  disc $J20$.

Hence the move $H18$ turns the $6$ vertical white discs in the 18th
file together with the one white disc $I19$ on the south–east
diagonal, i.e. $6+1=7$ white discs are turned over in the $8$ directions.
The new black disc makes eight discs change colour on the move.
The same number is obtained, e.g., on the empty square $M20$,

* $W$: $M19,W\;M18,W\;M17,W\;M16,B$,
* $NW$: $L19,W\;K18,W\;J17,W\;I16,B$,
* $SW$: $N19,W\;O18,B$,

$3+3+1=7$ white discs.  In particular a pure vertical capture is
obtained on $H18,H19$ etc. by the six white discs $I18\!-\!N18$ – $I19\!-\!N19$
in the 18th/19th file, i.e. six white discs can be taken in a straight
line and seven white discs in total on the best combined line move.
This is the maximal capture attainable from the position; with the
convention of counting the disc that is played the move changes eight
discs in total. ∎

In a legal Reversi move the newly played disc has to be flanked in at least
one of the eight orthogonal directions by a contiguous block of opponent
discs which is itself bounded by a disc of the player who is moving.  On
the 20$\times$20 board which is drawn here the only non trivial
contiguous blocks of White discs are the ones which are built up on the
right hand side of the board

* $I_{16}B\;I_{17}W\;I_{18}W\;I_{19}W\;I_{20}B$,
* $J_{15}B\;J_{16}B\;J_{17}W\;J_{18}W\;J_{19}W\;J_{20}W\;J_{21}W\;J_{22}B$,
* $K_{16}W\;K_{17}W\;K_{18}W\;K_{19}W\;K_{20}W$,
* $L_{16}W\;L_{17}W\;L_{18}W\;L_{19}W\;L_{20}W$,
* $M_{16}B\;M_{17}W\;M_{18}W\;M_{19}W$,
* $N_{16}B\;N_{17}W\;N_{18}W\;N_{19}W$,
* $O_{17}B\;O_{18}B\;O_{19}W$,

and the three isolated Black sentinels

$F_{17}B,\;G_{17}B,\;H_{17}B$.

The only squares which are empty and which lie on the same line as one
of the White blocks and which are bounded on the far side of the block
by a Black disc are the squares on the left hand side of the $K\!-\!L$ 
White strip.  Playing, e.g., in the conventional notation

$K15$

puts a Black disc immediately to the left of the five White discs

$K16W\;K17W\;K18W\;K19W\;K20W$

and the five discs are immediately flanked on the right by the Black
disc which is already present in the $J\!-\!O$ block.  The same square
is also on the same file as the six White discs

$I17W,J17W,K17W,L17W,M17W,N17W$

which are bounded on the north by the Black sentinel $H17B$ and on the
south by the Black disc $O17B$.  In the orthogonal directions the move
therefore turns

* $5$ White discs in the horizontal $K$–file,
* $6$ White discs in the vertical $17$–file,

the two directions being disjoint.  Up to the usual $+1$ for the disc
which is placed the move therefore turns $5+8=13$ White discs, i.e. $15$
discs counting the newly placed Black disc.  This is the longest
flanked block which occurs on the position and it is the usual way the
position is quoted, $15$ discs in total, $13$ White discs being actually
reversed.  In particular the $K15/L15$ family of moves is the unique
maximal move of the position; the often quoted "13 White reversals’’
is the same move written without the newly placed disc.  This is the
best that Black can do on the given custom board. ∎
